record.original_question: Can one prove in a representation-independent way that the geodesic-orbit property of a homogeneous space does not depend on the chosen coset presentation M = G/K or on the chosen Ad(K)-invariant reductive decomposition g = k + m, especially when one wants to show that the space is in no way naturally reductive?

evidence.quote: Another difficulty that one faces, is to show that the g.o. property of a homogeneous space (M = G/K, g) does not depend on the representation as a coset space and on the Ad(K)-invariant decomposition g = k ⊕ m, that is the space is in no way naturally reductive. Therefore, we often stress that we study G-g.o. spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a connected Riemannian homogeneous space. Recall that $(M,g)$ is called a geodesic orbit space (g.o. space) if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of the full isometry group $\mathrm{Isom}(M,g)$. Given any presentation $M = G/K$ as a coset space of a connected Lie group $G$ acting transitively by isometries, with isotropy subgroup $K$, and any $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ of the Lie algebras, one says that $(M,g)$ is $G$-naturally reductive (with respect to this decomposition) if 
$$\langle [X,Y]_{\mathfrak{m}}, Z\rangle + \langle Y, [X,Z]_{\mathfrak{m}}\rangle = 0 \qquad \text{for all } X,Y,Z \in \mathfrak{m},$$
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$ corresponding to $g_{eK}$. The space $(M,g)$ is said to be naturally reductive if it admits some transitive group $G$ of isometries and some $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive decomposition for which it is $G$-naturally reductive.

Develop a representation-independent criterion (i.e., one phrased intrinsically in terms of $(M,g)$, independent of the chosen transitive group $G$, the chosen isotropy $K$, and the chosen $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement $\mathfrak{m}$) that establishes whether the geodesic orbit property of $(M,g)$ holds, and in particular use this criterion to prove that a given geodesic orbit Riemannian homogeneous space $(M,g)$ is in no way naturally reductive — that is, there exist no transitive Lie group $G$ of isometries of $(M,g)$ and no $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive decomposition of $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the natural reductivity condition above is satisfied.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research articles on geodesic orbit (g.o.) manifolds (e.g., reviews of compact g.o. manifolds and works on Randers/spray g.o. spaces from 2020–2024) continue to treat the question of representation independence of the g.o. property and of natural reductivity case-by-case, typically by fixing a specific transitive group $G$ and emphasizing "$G$-g.o." spaces. No general representation-independent criterion appears to have been established, and showing that particular g.o. spaces are in no way naturally reductive is still handled on an ad hoc basis. The problem therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A review of compact geodesic orbit manifolds and the g.o. condition for SU(5)/S(U(2)×U(2))
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of g.o. manifolds emphasizes dependence on the chosen transitive group G and reductive decomposition.
status_evidence.claim: The classification and characterization of g.o. spaces is treated G-by-G, with the question of representation independence still being addressed case-by-case.

status_evidence.title: Arvanitoyeorgos, Homogeneous geodesics and geodesic orbit spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses naturally reductive and g.o. spaces relative to chosen reductive decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: The standard framework defines g.o. and naturally reductive properties relative to a fixed coset presentation and reductive complement.
